newsitem.title: SPAIN: American Airlines to buy 10 pct of Aero Argentinas.
newsitem.headline: American Airlines to buy 10 pct of Aero Argentinas.

text.p: Spanish flagship carrier Iberia said Friday that American Airlines will buy a 10 percent stake in Aerolineas Argentinas, the Argentine carrier that Iberia controls.
Iberia will retain 10 percent of the airline, while the remainder will be sold, it said.

As part of deals signed Friday with AMR Corp.'s American Airlines and British Airways, both carriers have an option to buy a minority stake in Iberia up until Dec. 31, state holding group Sociedad Estatal de Participaciones Industriales, or SEPI, said.

"The agreements, once developed, will permit Iberia to increase its offer of flights and international connections given the operation of flights with shared codes, and will coordinate its services to offer greater benefits to clients, in what will be one of the world's biggest networks of global routes," SEPI said in a statement.
In the deal with British Airways, Iberia will establish code-sharing and an agreement for frequent travelers.

The deal with American Airlines will also include "the establishment of flight code-sharing, the coordination of frequent-flying programmes, of cargo operations and of all areas where service could be improved," SEPI said.
American's participation in Aerolineas Argentinas will be translated into code-sharing agreements and the coordination of products and services.

SEPI said the deal will "strengthen (Iberia's) market position at home, assuring and extending its leadership in traffic between Europe and Latin America, as well as increasing its presence in the European, North Atlantic and Asian markets."
For Aerolineas, the deal was its best alternative for it to compete in the U.S. and Argentine market, which makes up 25 percent of its business, SEPI said.
